newsitem.title: USA: Amdahl sees tight Millennium supplies.
newsitem.headline: Amdahl sees tight Millennium supplies.

text.p: Amdahl Corp Monday reiterated that supplies of its Millennium mainframes will be somewhat constrained until it completes ramping up production late in the fourth quarter.
In a statement accompanying its third quarter results, Amdahl Chairman John Lewis said Amdahl began shipping limited numbers of its new mainframes in the third quarter.

"Those new Millennium processors have been performing well at the early customer sites," he said, adding that Amdahl expects to increase production volumes and make the products generally available during the fourth quarter.
In the third quarter, the company also announced some additional Millennium models designed for medium-sized computing requirements.
"These should complement the larger Millennium systems already announced and allow us to serve a broader segment of the market," Lewis said.

Amdahl earlier reported a third-quarter loss of $4,833,000 or $0.04 a share on revenues of $439,819,000. That compared to net income of $20,057,000 or $0.17 a share and revenues of $350,016,000 in the same period a year ago.

Lewis said the loss continues to reflect reduced revenues and margins from the sale of International Business Machines Corp -compatible products. In the second quarter, Amdahl took nonrecurring charges of $150.7 million or $1.25 a share including a $130-million writedown in the value of its older mainframe computer assets which have come under extreme pricing pressure during a transition to new products.
